newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says CL SDBO buy-back contains no aid.
newsitem.headline: EU says CL SDBO buy-back contains no aid.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday that Credit Lyonnais's (CL) buy-back of Societe de Banque Occidentale (SDBO) did not involve any state subsidies.

The Commission queried in September 1996 the price of 50 million francs paid by CL for its former banking subsidiary after it was recapitalised by CDR, the state-backed vehicle charged with restructuring CL's loss-making assets.
It said at the time that there were suspicions that Lyonnais had paid much less than the market value. But Commission state aid officials said those suspicions turned out to be groundless.
"The French authorities proved Credit Lyonnais paid the right market price for SDBO," one official said.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the Commission said that the French authorities had clarified that SDBO's capital had been increased by 240.5 million francs not 274.5 million francs as Brussels initially thought.

The Commission's September probe therefore only concerned 190.5 million francs injected into SDBO -- which is the difference between the actual 240.5-million capital increase and the 50 millions paid by Lyonnais to regain control of SDBO.
